I'll think through this as the farmer, then give my plan.

My 12 mu is split. I keep 6 mu in cotton — that's my main crop, been doing it same way for years. The other 6 mu I do winter wheat then summer maize, two harvests a year. That's how most folks around here run their land.

For the cotton, I plant Bt hybrid seed — the kind that handles bollworm better. Saved me a lot of spraying since I switched. I still spray maybe 5-6 times for aphids, spider mites, and late-season bollworm that the Bt doesn't catch well. Last year I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer (50 jin, 15-15-15) as base, plus one bag of urea at squaring. That works out to roughly 18 kg N per mu. I use well water — cotton needs watering maybe 2-3 times, at squaring and flowering. Got about 270 kg seed cotton per mu last year, I'll aim for similar.

For wheat, I sow Jimai variety in October. I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu before plowing, then topdress urea in spring when it greens up. Comes to about 28 kg N. I water 2 times — once before winter, once at jointing. Spray twice for aphids and powdery mildew. I get around 480 kg/mu most years.

For summer maize after wheat, I direct-drill right after wheat harvest in June — no-till saves time and moisture. Zhengdan 958 or similar. About 22 kg N, some at sowing, rest at big trumpet stage. One irrigation usually, sometimes two if dry. Spray once for borer. Gets me 550 kg/mu.

My wife and I handle most work; kids work in town. I rent a harvester for wheat and maize. Cotton picking is still by hand — family helps at weekends.
